You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import numpy as np
for p in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3']:
    inp=np.array(G[p+' input']); out=np.array(G[p+' output'])
    H,W=inp.shape
    rows=set(inp[:,0]) | None
    # pure separator rows: entirely one color
    def sepcols(cols):
        c=np.where(np.all(inp[0,:]==inp[0,:] & False if False else True,axis=None)[0])
        return c
    # find rows/cols constant
    const_rows=[r for r in range(H) if len(set(inp[r,:]))==1]
    const_cols=[c for c in range(W) if len(set(inp[:,c]))==1]
    mark_colors=[c for c in np.unique(inp) if c!=inp[0,0]]
    print(p,'const rows',const_rows,'const cols',const_cols)
    for c in mark_colors:
        pts=np.argwhere(inp==c)
        print('   color',c,len(pts),'positions rows',sorted(pts[:,0]),'cols',sorted(pts[:,1]))
    print('   out dims',out.shape)

def const_lines(g):
    g=np.array(g); H,W=g.shape

    def bmap(L,n):
        pts=set(L); segs=[]; prev=-1
        for p in sorted(pts):

def tiles(g,out_h,out_w):
    g=np.array(g); oh,ow=out_h,out_w
    H,W=g.shape
    rh=[round(H*i/oh) for i in range(oh+1)]; rw=[round(W*j/ow) for j in range(ow+1)]
    return [(rh[a],rh[b+1]) for a,b in zip(range(oh),range(oh))] if False else None
def get_tiles(g,oh,ow):
    g=np.array(g); H,W=g.shape
    rs=[round(H*i/oh) for i in range(oh+1)]; cs=[round(W*j/ow) for j in range(ow+1)]

    inp=np.array(G[p+' input']); out=np.array(G[p+' output'])

import numpy as np, collections
def solve(g):
    g=np.array(g); H,W=g.shape
    vals=collections.Counter(g.flatten().tolist()); bg=int(vals.most_common(1)[0][0])
    # unique marker row/col coords
    mr=[r for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r,c]!=bg]
    mc=[c for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r,c]!=bg]
    ur=sorted(set(mr)); uc=sorted(set(mc))
    R=[(ur[i],ur[i+1]) for i in range(len(ur)-1)]
    C=[(uc[j],uc[j+1]) for j in range(len(uc)-1)]
    out=[]
    for rlo,rhi in R:
        row=[]
        for clo,chi in C:
            cells=[(rr,cc,int(g[rr,cc])) for rr in range(rlo+1,rhi) for cc in range(clo+1,chi) if g[rr,cc]!=bg]
            if cells: row.append(cells[0][2]); 
            elif g[rlo,rlo]!=bg: row.append(int(g[rlo,rlo])); 
            else: row.append(bg)
        out.append(row)
    return out
for p in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3']:
    got=solve(G[p+' input'])
    exp=G[p+' output']
    print(p,'MATCH' if got==exp else 'MISMATCH',got)

import os,re,numpy as np,collections,itertools
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
for p in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3','Demo pair 4']:
    g=np.array(G[p+' input']); out=np.array(G[p+' output'])
    mr=[r for r in range(g.shape[0]) for c in range(g.shape[1]) if g[r,c]!=collections.Counter(map(int,g.flatten())).most_common(1)[0][0] and g[r,c]!=None]
    # marker coordinates of colored points (non-bg) with their color
    cc=collections.Counter(map(int,g.flatten()))
    bgv=int(cc.most_common(1)[0][0])
    pts=[(r,c,int(g[r,c])) for r in range(g.shape[0]) for c in range(g.shape[1]) if int(g[r,c])!=bgv]
    mr=sorted(set(pts[:,0])); mc=sorted(set(pts[:,1]))
    print('---',p,'shape',g.shape,'out',out.shape,'mr',mr,'mc',mc)
    def gaps(xs): return len(xs)-1 if xs else 0
    print('   rowgaps',gaps(mr),'markercols',gaps(mc),'outshape',(out.shape))

import os,re,numpy as np,collections
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
for p in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2']:
    g=np.array(G[p+' input']); out=np.array(G[p+' output']); H,W=g.shape
    cnt=collections.Counter(map(int,g.flatten())); bg=int(cnt.most_common(1)[0][0])
    pts=[(r,c,int(g[r,c])) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r,c]!=bg]
    mr=set(r for r,_,_ in pts); mc=set(c for _,c,_ in pts)
    rcnt=len(mr); ccnt=len(mc)
    print('---',p,'bg',bg,'out',out.shape,'distinct mr',rcnt,'mc',ccnt)
    print('  out:',out)
    # where do marker colors sit relative to out? print rows/cols of markers by color sorted
    bycol=collections.defaultdict(list)
    for r,c,v in pts: bycol[v].append((r,c))
    for v in sorted(set(v for _,_,v in pts)):
        rs=sorted(p[0] for p in bycol[v]); cs=sorted(p[1] for p in bycol[v])
        print('   color',v,'nr',len(rs),'nc',len(cs),'rs ranges',min(rs),max(rs))

import numpy as np, collections
def parts(g, sep_color):
    g=np.array(g)
    H,W=g.shape
    # find colors forming full uniform rows
    rows=[r for r in range(H) if len(set(map(int,g[r,:])))==1]
    # markers: cells with colors different from bg and sep-color
    vals=collections.Counter(map(int,g.flatten()))
    bg=int(vals.most_common(1)[0][0])
    mk=set(v for v in vals if v!=bg and v!=sep_color)
    mks=[(r,c,int(g[r,c])) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if int(g[r,c]) in mk]
    return rows,mks,bg
for p,sc in [('Demo pair 1',5),('Demo pair 2',1),('Demo pair 4',5)]:
    g=G[p+' input']
    rows,mks,bg=parts(g,sc)
    print(p,'bg',bg,'sep rows',rows,'markers',mks)

import numpy as np, collections
def analyze(p):
    g=np.array(G[p+' input']); o=np.array(G[p+' output'])
    H,W=g.shape
    vals=collections.Counter(map(int,g.flatten()))
    bg=int(vals.most_common(1)[0][0])
    # find uniform lines of non-bg color
    nonbg=[v for v in vals if v!=bg]
    # uniform full rows / cols of a single non-bg color
    lines=[]
    for r in range(H):
        if len(set(map(int,g[r,:])))==1 and not any(x==bg for x in g[r,:]):
            lines.append(('r',r,int(g[0,r])))
    for c in range(W):
        col=g[:,c]
        if len(set(map(int,col)))==1 and not any(x==bg for x in col):
            lines.append(('c',c,int(col[0])))
    print(p,'H,W',H,W,'bg',bg,'uniform-lines',lines,'out',o.shape)
    return g,o,bg,nonbg,lines
for p in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 4']:
    analyze(p)

import os,re,numpy as np,collections
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G

    H,W=g.shape

        pts=list(sorted(set(map(int,indices))+bounds))

import numpy as np, collections
def load(): return G
g=np.array(G['Demo pair 5 input'])
H,W=g.shape
# row separators: full rows of 4
sr=[r for r in range(H) if np.all(g[r]==4)]
print('rowsep',sr)
# output 5x4 -> 5 row-bands, 4 col-bands.
# Try: band boundaries at consecutive row-seps + borders? sr=[4,9,14,19,24,29]
# 6 rows -> 5 interior gaps? out has 5 rows. Bands: [0,3],[5,8],[10,13],[15,18],[20,23] = 5 bands (exclude last block after 29)
rb=[(0,3),(5,8),(10,13),(15,18),(20,23)]
# col bands? out has 4 cols. Marker cols in each row: row4:[2,7], row9:[2,7,17,22], row14:[2,7,12,17,22]
# Guess: col separators = columns containing any marker (2,7,12,17,22) giving 6 bands; but out 4 cols.
# Alternative: group by distance? Let's print markers per band-row with column
mks=[(r,c,int(v)) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) for v in [int(g[r,c])] if int(g[r,c])!=8 and int(g[r,c])!=4]
from collections import defaultdict
byr=defaultdict(set); byc=defaultdict(set)
for r,c,v in mks: byr[r].add(v); byc[c].add(v)
print('per row',sorted(byr.items()))
print('per col',sorted(byc.items()))

import os,glob,re
d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
    k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
    rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
    if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
        G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
print(sorted(G))
inp=G.get('Test input')
print(inp if inp is not None else 'none')

from collections import Counter
def info(gi, go):
    c=Counter(x for r in gi for x in r)
    bg=c.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # second most common = line
    mc=c.most_common()
    line=mc[1][0] if len(mc)>1 else None
    return bg,line,c,go
for i in [1,2,3,4,5]:
    gi=G[f'Demo pair {i} input']; go=G[f'Demo pair {i} output']

    # separator lines: full rows or cols of the line color

import os,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()

def analyze(gi):
    c=Counter(x for r in gi for x in r)
    mc=c.most_common(); bg=mc[0][0]
    # line = separator lines' color: color appearing in long straight runs; pick non-bg with max count among those
    others=[v for v,_ in mc[1:]]
    # heuristic: line color forms the dense lattice; it's the second most common overall usually
    line=others[0] if len(others)>1 else None
    return bg,line,gi

    rcR=[b1,b2+1 for b1,b2 in zip([-1]+scR, scR+[w])]
    print('demo',i,'bg',bg,'line',line_,'out',len(go),'x',len(go[0]))

from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import os,re

def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()

for i in range(1,6):
    gi=G[f'Demo pair {i} input']; go=G[f'Demo pair {i} output']
    h,w=len(gi),len(gi[0])
    c=Counter(x for r in gi for x in r)
    mc=c.most_common(); bg=mc[0][0]
    line_=max((v,count) for v,count in mc[1:])
    markers=[]
    for r in range(h):
        for cc in range(w):
            if gi[r][cc] not in (bg,line_):
                markers.append((gi[r][cc],r,cc))
    rs=sorted({p[1] for p in markers}); cs=sorted({p[2] for p in markers})
    rh=len(rs)-1 if len(rs)>1 else (1 if len(rs)==1 else 0)
    cw=len(cs)-1 if len(cs)>1 else (1 if len(cs)==1 else 0)
    def idx(x,xs): return xs.index(x) if x in xs else None
    out_pred=[[None]*cw for _ in range(rh)]
    for v,r,cc in markers:
        ri,idxr=idx(r,rs) if rh>0 else (0,-1)
        ci,idxc=idx(cc,cs) if cw>0 else (0,-1)
        if 0<=ri<rh and 0<=ci<cw:
            out_pred[ri][ci]=(v,)
    pred_ok = all(out_pred[j][i]==go[j][i] for j in range(len(go)) for i in range(len(go[0])))
    print(f'demo {i}: dims ({rh}x{cw}) pred_correct={pred_ok}')
